# Caligrafy Quill

> Caligrafy Quill is an open-source PHP MVC framework (PHP 8.3+, MySQL, Pug views, Vue 3 client apps, MIT) made for coding agents. You write each feature once as a capability (a `Caligrafy\Service` class with `#[Capability]`), and the framework serves it to web pages, forms, a REST API, a generated JS client for Vue apps, iOS and Android apps (`php caligrafer.php mobile`, `Route::mobile`), AI agents over MCP and Snap Cards. Its slogan is "Describe it. Approve it. Ship it.": with Claude Code, `/caligrafy-quill:idea` turns an idea into a complete app online at `https://<name>.caligrafy.com`.

Rules an agent must follow in a Caligrafy project:

- Only capabilities touch models. Requests are declared in `application/config/routing/web.php`: `Route::page()` (a page with data from capabilities), `Route::form()`, `Route::auth()`, `Route::webhook()`, `Route::download()`, `Route::capability()` / `Route::capabilities()` (REST), `Route::mcp()` (agents), `Route::snap()` (cards and the assistant), and `Route::action()` on a `webOnly: true` capability for anything else. Do not write new controllers.
- In a capability, declare every input in `$rules`, return data from `handle(array $input, Context $context)`, and refuse with `ServiceError`. Never render, redirect, print or read the session there.
- Read data with the query builder (`Book::where('author_id', $id)->with('author')->paginate(20)`, `Database::table()`) or with bound `?` queries. Never concatenate request data into SQL.
- A change to a table that already holds data is a migration (`php caligrafer.php migrate make <name>`).
- Pug views are compiled to PHP, so strings join with `.`, never `+`.
- Never put API keys or tokens in pages or bundles. Never print or commit `.env` secrets.
- Exact signatures are in the API reference, and the verified pitfalls (G1-G187) are in the gotchas. Read them before writing code.

A minimal capability (`application/services/Bookshelf/ListBooks.php`):

```php
#[Capability(name: 'list_books', description: 'Lists the books, 20 per page, each with its author.', scope: 'books:read', readOnly: true, public: true)]
class ListBooks extends Service
{
    public $rules = array('author_id' => 'integer', 'page' => 'integer');
    public function handle(array $input, Context $context)
    {
        $query = Book::with('author')->orderBy('title');
        if (!empty($input['author_id'])) { $query->where('author_id', $input['author_id']); }
        return $query->paginate(20, $input['page'] ?? 1);
    }
}
```

Served everywhere from `web.php`: `Route::page('/books', 'Bookshelf/books', ['data' => ['books' => 'list_books']]);`, `Route::capability('GET', '/api/books', 'list_books');` and `Route::mcp('/mcp');`.
